caption: What if the Moon vanished for just 5 seconds? It's about 384,400 km away, so its light takes about 1.3 seconds to reach us. You'd keep seeing it for 1.3 seconds after it was gone. Its gravity would switch off late too: in 2017, the neutron-star merger GW170817 showed gravity travels at the speed of light. Moonlight is just reflected sunlight, so the night would dim. The Moon drives most of our tides (the Sun's pull is about 46% as strong), but oceans take hours to respond, so 5 seconds changes almost nothing. Scientists bounce lasers off mirrors Apollo astronauts left on the Moon. India's Chandrayaan-3 lander carries a NASA laser reflector too. Would YOU have noticed? 👇
